scope: Original installed Edge extension; one public word request before and one after the fix, plus one baseline public sentence request.

publicSample.context: Go is efficient, scalable, and productive.

measurementDefinitions.origin: performance.now immediately before sending translate through the extension Port; includes local settings and permission checks.
measurementDefinitions.startedMs: Receipt of the background started event after settings and permission checks, immediately before provider execution.
measurementDefinitions.progressMs: Receipt of the first provider progress event caused by a valid model SSE choice, including a role-only event; not time to a translation token.
measurementDefinitions.firstPreviewMs: Receipt of the first word-preview with a nonempty, closed translation field.
measurementDefinitions.contextReadyMs: Receipt of enough word-preview fields to contain nonempty translation, partOfSpeech, and explanation.
measurementDefinitions.resultMs: Receipt of the fully parsed and validated final result.
measurementDefinitions.paint: Port event timing only; does not measure rendered DOM or a painted browser frame.
measurementDefinitions.network: No direct DNS, TLS, response-header, or server-compute measurement was taken.

limits: Each condition has only one sample. Service load, network conditions, and upstream caching vary between calls, so these measurements do not establish a model or network speedup.

The final dictionary duration stayed approximately 1.6 seconds. The observed improvement is that connection waiting ends on a real model event and the contextual meaning arrives before the remaining senses finish.
Baseline provider emitted no word delta or preview events, so progress and preview timings are unavailable for the baseline rather than measured as zero.
The unusually long wait described by the user was not reproduced during these three requests.
The reported apiAccess and webAccess booleans stayed unchanged; the probe did not enumerate the complete browser permission collection.
